public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 163

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/163](https://www.erdosproblems.com/163)
- [BuEr75] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P., On the Ramsey number of graphs with small degree-ratio.
  Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai (1975).
- [Le17] Lee, C., Ramsey numbers of degenerate graphs. Ann. of Math. (2) 185 (2017), 791-829.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos163

/--
The Burr-Erdős conjecture: For any $d\geq 1$ if $H$ is a graph such that every subgraph
contains a vertex of degree at most $d$ then
$$R(H)\ll_d n.$$

Solved by Lee [Le17], who proved that $R(H) \leq 2^{2^{O(d)}}n$.

This problem is #9 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol) gives, for graphs `H` on `Fin n`, a natural
constant `C ≥ 1` with `RamseyFor H (C * n)` (every red/blue colouring of `K_{C n}` contains a
monochromatic copy of `H`); transporting along `Fintype.equivFin` gives the statement below.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos163.lean#L53"]
theorem erdos_163 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ d →
      ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (H : SimpleGraph V),
        H.IsDegenerate d →
        (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey H : ℝ) ≤ C * Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos163

findings.description: The bibliography at lines 25–26 gives [BuEr75] the title “On the Ramsey number of graphs with small degree-ratio.” The Burr–Erdős paper cited for this conjecture is actually titled “On the magnitude of generalized Ramsey numbers for graphs.” This is a reference error; the mathematical statement is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The original paper’s first page (printed p. 215) bears the title “ON THE MAGNITUDE OF GENERALIZED RAMSEY NUMBERS FOR GRAPHS”; p. 216 states the bounded-arboricity conjecture. See https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-26.pdf. The UCSD Linear Ramsey problem collection, reference [8], and Lee’s bibliography also give this title.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [BuEr75] title with “On the magnitude of generalized Ramsey numbers for graphs,” retaining the 1975 publication year and Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai reference.

reformulations.difference: The source tests all nonempty subgraphs for a vertex of degree at most d; Lean’s IsDegenerate tests nonempty finite vertex sets and counts neighbours in the corresponding induced subgraph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite graphs these conditions are equivalent. The source’s condition applies to every induced subgraph. Conversely, apply IsDegenerate to the vertex set of an arbitrary nonempty subgraph K. The resulting vertex has at most d neighbours in the induced graph, and deleting edges to obtain K cannot increase its degree. Both the predicate equivalence and the resulting equivalence of the quantified Ramsey statements were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization found. The uniform constant, quantifier scope, ordinary non-induced graph copies, and affirmative answer match the sources. Lean checks proved R(edgeless V) = |V|, including the empty and singleton cases, and proved that the set defining the Ramsey infimum is nonempty. The exact linked formal proof rebuilt successfully; its theorem has only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound as axioms. A separate scratch proof in /workspace/review/bridge.lean verifies that its natural-constant/Fin-n statement implies the repository’s real-constant/arbitrary-finite-type statement. The research-solved tag and formal_proof record are supported.
